subject: Concordia Therapeutics - request for multi-year price anchoring & renewal protection
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@concordia.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: David Ruiz <david.ruiz@concordia.com>, Paul Simmons <psimmons@concordia.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring 3-year program: price stability and renewal protections

Hannah — thanks again for the demo last week. Concordia's exec team is energized about embedding Redwood for our core product inference. Two procurement items came up that we need to lock before we move to contracting: a multi-year price anchor (3 years) and an explicit uplift cap on year-over-year increases, plus a renewal protection clause that ensures a defined negotiation window and no unilateral price jumps.

High level asks: 
- Price lock for 36 months on the committed SKU mix
- Uplift cap <= 8% per year (absolute)
- Renewal protection: 90-day negotiation window, no automatic price increases above agreed-upon uplift cap; ability to terminate if material change to T&Cs

We can share an updated SOW and expected usage tiers (attached). Can your team confirm whether Redwood can provide an approval path for these non-standard terms?

Attachments: Concordia_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, usage tiers)

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Procurement
Concordia Therapeutics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@concordia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring 3-year program: price stability and renewal protections

Ellen — really appreciate the clear asks and the SOW. Quick summary from our side: the commercial team is open to multi-year anchors for committed capacity, but the exact uplift cap and renewal language require Deal Desk + executive sign-off given the duration and potential margin impact. I've looped in Jordan (Deal Desk) and Laura (Rev Ops) to outline a recommended guardrail.

Proposed internal path: 
1) Jordan to assess financial exposure and propose a limited exception (pricing bands, break-points).
2) If Deal Desk supports, we'll route to Laura for an exec-level signoff (may require partial credit or an annual minimum commitment).
3) We can provide a clean MSA/SOW with explicit uplift cap and renewal negotiation window; legal redlines to follow.

I'll prioritize a rapid review — Concordia is strategic and the usage profile looks attractive. Will confirm next steps by EOD tomorrow.

— Hannah

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring 3-year program: price stability and renewal protections

Team — reviewed Concordia's expected tiers and modeled a few scenarios. Notes below (TL;DR at the top):

TL;DR: Recommend a conditional 36-month anchor with a maximum annual uplift of 8% (cap applies only to published per-unit list price increases; effective price may vary with committed volume bands). Require 12-month minimum billing commitment + break fee tiered on remaining term if Concordia reduces committed capacity below agreed floors. Approve contingent on finance sign-off and a one-time onboarding credit to protect margins in year 1.

Details: 
- Exposure: If usage skews heavy to peak tokens beyond the committed tiers, uplift economics degrade quickly. To mitigate, exception should include clear commitment bands and overage pricing that is more aggressive (higher) than the committed rate.
- Uplift cap: 8% max is acceptable as a negotiated guardrail but we should keep carve-outs for material changes in cloud costs, regulatory obligations, or required security controls (we can add a formulaic pass-through clause).
- Renewal protection: 90-day negotiation window OK. Add explicit language that prevents automatic price increases exceeding the uplift cap without mutual written consent. Add right to terminate if Redwood introduces changes that materially reduce functionality or increase costs beyond a defined threshold.
- Legal redlines: Concordia's team already provided a draft with a broad 'price stability' clause — we should tighten definitions (committed SKU mix, measurement windows, and mid-term change triggers).

Action requested: Laura/Finance — please greenlight the recommended exception (36m anchor, 8% uplift cap, 12m minimum billing, one-time onboarding credit of $45k) or provide alternate parameters. If approved, I'll prepare the final commercial terms and redlines to send to Concordia.

Attachments referenced: Concordia_MA&P_3yr_term_redlines.docx (internal redline suggestions)

— Jordan

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring 3-year program: price stability and renewal protections

Jordan/Team — reviewed the exposure and the recommended guardrails. I will approve the commercial exception with the following conditions: 

1) Price lock: 36 months for the committed SKU mix as defined in the attached SOW.
2) Uplift cap: 8% per year maximum, but any pass-through for material third-party cost increases will be explicitly capped at CPI + 3% and require 30-day notice.
3) Renewal protection: 90-day negotiation window; add an "exception review" clause that triggers a senior-review by Rev Ops if requested changes exceed a 12% aggregate deviation across committed SKUs.
4) Billing minimum: 12-month minimum billing commitment. Break fees as Jordan proposed.
5) Onboarding concession: Approve a one-time onboarding credit of $35k (reduced from $45k) to balance margin impact.

Final ask: Jordan to add the above to the commercial memo and provide an updated MOP and a short exec summary for COO sign-off (we need COO approval because this exceeds standard exception thresholds). Laura will route to COO with the exec summary; please put the HubSpot deal id and a projected ARR delta on the summary.

I'll sign off on the revised MSA once legal confirms language around pass-through and termination triggers.

— Laura

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@concordia.com>
Cc: David Ruiz <david.ruiz@concordia.com>, Paul Simmons <psimmons@concordia.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring 3-year program: price stability and renewal protections

Ellen — appreciate the patience while we evaluated. Good news: we've secured internal approval to move forward on a 36-month price anchor with an 8% maximum annual uplift and the 90-day renewal negotiation window you requested. A few important details to note before we finalize redlines: 

- We will include a 12-month billing minimum and a tiered break fee schedule that protects Redwood from abrupt decommitment.
- Pass-throughs for material third-party or regulatory-driven cost increases will be limited to CPI + 3% with a 30-day notice requirement.
- Our legal team will tighten definitions around "committed SKU mix" and add an "exception review" trigger for changes that exceed 12% aggregate deviation.
- As a balancing concession, Concordia will receive a one-time onboarding credit of $35,000 applied to the first invoice.

I'm attaching the updated MOP and a redline-ready MSA for your review. If Concordia is comfortable, can we agree to a DocuSign request by EOW next week so legal can close?

Attachments: Concordia_MA&P_3yr_term_redlines.docx, Concordia_SOW_v3.pdf

Thanks again — excited to get this over the line.

— Hannah
